registryLegalName: Solicitor Application to Destroy Arrest Records After Successful Traffic Education Program Completion, S.C. Code § 17-22-330(A)

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: On successful completion of a traffic education programme the administering governmental agency shall effect a noncriminal disposition of the offence, with no record maintained except by the programme to prevent a second use.

Each circuit solicitor has prosecutorial discretion to establish a traffic education programme for persons who commit traffic-related offences punishable only by a fine and loss of four points or less, and participation is barred where the offence resulted in death or serious bodily injury.
Eligibility is confined to a person with no significant history of traffic violations, and participation is allowed only once.
Allows termination and reinstatement of the offence for violating the conditions of the programme.
Requires termination where the person receives a subsequent traffic violation in the six months following the ticket.
Names the traffic education program director as an attestor for the expungement paperwork.
Subsection (E)(1) exempts § 17-22-330(A) from the SLED verification fee.

counselFlags: South Carolina expungements start with either the Solicitor's Office or the summary court and use the official SCCA 223-series forms. LegalEase must not produce a substitute for an official South Carolina Judicial Branch form.
South Carolina generally expunges one charge per order, with special fee-treatment rules for related charges arising from the same incident under the Uniform Expungement Act.

A pardon is a separate process through the Department of Probation, Parole and Pardon Services and is NOT expungement. Do not file a pardon as an expungement and do not tell a participant that a pardon clears the record.

Destruction-application provision not established: the source describes § 17-22-330(A), (C) and (D) but does not reproduce a subsection providing the application to destroy records, and § 17-22-350 appears in the authority list without its text being read. The statutory hook for the destruction application on this track must be confirmed before any instrument is built.

Waiting period: none beyond successful completion of the traffic education programme and the noncriminal disposition under § 17-22-330(A). Note that a subsequent traffic violation within six months of the ticket terminates the programme and reinstates the offence.
No verification or notarization statute is identified for the § 17-22-330 route. Verification is a feature of the official SCCA form, which is not drafted here; nothing is filled.
Eligibility is narrow: traffic-related offences punishable only by a fine and loss of four points or less, no significant history of traffic violations, and participation only once.
Any offence that resulted in death or serious bodily injury to another person is barred from the programme.

The programme terminates and the offence is reinstated where the participant receives a subsequent traffic violation within six months of the ticket, or otherwise violates the conditions. Screening must confirm this has not happened before any relief is described.

Attestation: § 17-22-940(D) names the traffic education program director as an attestor. That attestation is obtained from the programme, and LegalEase never attests completion or asserts that it occurred.
The SLED verification fee is not charged for this route under § 17-22-940(E)(1).

registryExcerpt.venue: Statewide statute administered circuit by circuit under the direct supervision and control of the circuit solicitor, who may contract with a county or municipality. Apply to the Solicitor's Office in the judicial circuit where the offence was committed.
registryExcerpt.destinationName: Solicitor's Office in the judicial circuit where the offence was committed

waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond successful completion and the noncriminal disposition under § 17-22-330(A). Note that a subsequent traffic violation within six months of the ticket terminates the programme and reinstates the offence.

exclusions: Any traffic-related offence not punishable only by a fine and loss of four points or less.
Any offence that resulted in death or serious bodily injury to another person.
Any person with a significant history of traffic violations.
Any second participation; § 17-22-320(A) allows the programme only once.
Any participant terminated for violating the conditions, or terminated because of a subsequent traffic violation within six months of the ticket.
